claim: the age gate's open-question exemption admits a class that performs no better than the rows the gate already blocks
privacy: AGGREGATES ONLY. The graded units and every replayed prompt are the maintainer's own transcripts and are never committed. Counts and intervals are reproducible from the harness; the text is not shareable.

index_composition.note: superseded_by is also set by typed supersedes links, so rows with an actual logged resolution are <= the reported count — conservative in the direction that weakens the finding

blind_grading.sample: deterministic, seed 491, drawn from exemption-admitted injections in a snapshot-correct harness replay; ages 8-42d, median 18
blind_grading.judge: blind to the hypothesis, to arm structure, and to any prior grading; wrote verdicts before the key was opened
blind_grading.interpretation: 10% sits inside the 6-10% band the gate already blocks for stale rows. The 40% bar originally pre-registered is NOT used: it is not derivable from anything measured, and the gate admits the 2-7d band at ~24%, so 40% held exempt rows to a higher standard than the policy applies to rows it keeps.

carry_depth.verdict: separates the WRONG way — the exempt class is the more re-asserted one

frontier_by_content.verdict: would gate 67 of 68, indistinguishable from removal, and points the same wrong way
frontier_by_content.caveat: recall.suggest does not SELECT frontier (only search does), so this describes a hypothetical column, not shipped behaviour

corpus_effect.note: purely subtractive at the prompt level. The instrument measures precision of what IS injected and is structurally blind to the value of what is now withheld.

not_measured: relevance of the 38 prompts' lost injections (the silence cost)
whether the pinned exemption earns its keep — it fires zero times on this corpus, so it rests on #452's original observation
13 of the suppressed rows are <=7d old and were lost to per-session origin cooldown divergence rather than to the gate; filed separately
